title: Move the password into .env
summary: The password is typed into compose.yaml twice. Put it in .env, use ${DB_PASSWORD}, change it, and get past the first-start catch.

tasks.title: `.env` sets `DB_PASSWORD` to a new password (not `secret`)
tasks.hint: Make a file called `.env` next to `compose.yaml` with one line, like `DB_PASSWORD=mango-lassi-7`.

tasks.title: `compose.yaml` says `${DB_PASSWORD}` in both places, and `secret` nowhere
tasks.hint: Replace both `secret`s with `${DB_PASSWORD}`. `docker compose config | grep -i password` shows the filled-in values.

tasks.title: The running `api` and `db` both got the password from `.env`
tasks.hint: `docker compose up -d` makes new containers with the new settings. If `api` and `db` disagree, one of them wasn't recreated.

tasks.title: `http://localhost:3502` works again, with no red error
tasks.hint: The page says `28P01`? That's Postgres's code for "wrong password". Postgres set its password on its first start and saved it in the volume; a new `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` is ignored after that. Start the database over: `docker compose down -v`, then `docker compose up -d`.
